FirstOrder.Language.Hom.toFun.fullDefinition: toFun : M → N   /-- The homomorphism commutes with the interpretations of the function symbols -/   -- Porting note:   -- The autoparam here used to be `obviously`. We would like to replace it with `aesop`   -- but that isn't currently sufficient.   -- See https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/287929-mathlib4/topic/Aesop.20and.20cases   -- If that can be improved, we should change this to `by aesop` and remove the proofs below.   map_fun' : ∀ {n} (f : L.Functions n) (x), toFun (funMap f x) = funMap f (toFun ∘ x) := by     intros; trivial   /-- The homomorphism sends related elements to related elements -/   map_rel' : ∀ {n} (r : L.Relations n) (x), RelMap r x → RelMap r (toFun ∘ x) := by     -- Porting note: see porting note on `Hom.map_fun'`     intros; trivial

FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.mk.injEq.{u, v, w, w'} {L : Language} {M : Type w} {N : Type w'} [L.Structure M]
  [L.Structure N] (toEquiv : M ≃ N)
  (map_fun' :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (f : L.Functions n) (x : Fin n → M), toEquiv.toFun (funMap f x) = funMap f (toEquiv.toFun ∘ x) := by
    intros; trivial)
  (map_rel' : ∀ {n : ℕ} (r : L.Relations n) (x : Fin n → M), RelMap r (toEquiv.toFun ∘ x) ↔ RelMap r x := by intros;
    trivial) :
  ∀ (toEquiv_1 : M ≃ N)
    (map_fun'_1 :
      autoParam
        (∀ {n : ℕ} (f : L.Functions n) (x : Fin n → M), toEquiv_1.toFun (funMap f x) = funMap f (toEquiv_1.toFun ∘ x))
        _auto✝)
    (map_rel'_1 :
      autoParam (∀ {n : ℕ} (r : L.Relations n) (x : Fin n → M), RelMap r (toEquiv_1.toFun ∘ x) ↔ RelMap r x) _auto✝¹),
    ({ toEquiv := toEquiv, map_fun' := map_fun', map_rel' := map_rel' } =
        { toEquiv := toEquiv_1, map_fun' := map_fun'_1, map_rel' := map_rel'_1 }) =
      (toEquiv = toEquiv_1)

explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Hom.comp_apply: The theorem demonstrates that composing two homomorphisms and then applying the result to an element is equivalent to applying the second homomorphism to the result of the first homomorphism applied to that element.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.toFun: An embedding is characterized as a function that maps elements from one set to another while preserving injectivity.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Embedding.map_rel': The theorem states that a relation is preserved under a homomorphism if related elements in one structure map to related elements in another structure through that homomorphism.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Embedding.map_fun: The theorem states that a homomorphic embedding preserves the evaluation of functions, meaning that applying a function to elements in one structure is equivalent to first mapping those elements to another structure and then applying the function.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Embedding.map_rel: The theorem states that for a relation in a language, the mapping of a relation under an embedding between structures is equivalent to the relation itself when evaluated at two different interpretations.

explanatories.Equiv.toFun: This definition specifies a function that retrieves the mapping from one type to another represented by an equivalence relation.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.map_rel': The theorem demonstrates that a relation mapping is preserved under a structure-preserving bijection between two models of a language.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.toEquiv: The definition describes a way to construct an equivalence between two structures of a language, capturing their relationship in a way that reflects the structure's properties.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.map_fun: The theorem establishes that under a language equivalence, the interpretation of a function applied to an argument from one structure is equal to applying the function to the image of the argument under the equivalence.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.map_rel: The theorem shows that a relation holds for a composed mapping of elements in one structure if and only if it holds for the original elements in another structure when there is a structure-preserving bijection between them.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.trans: This theorem demonstrates that in a transitive relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second and from the second to the third, it must also hold from the first element to the third.

FirstOrder.Language.LHom.defaultExpansio.fullDefinition: noncomputable def defaultExpansion (ϕ : L →ᴸ L')     [∀ (n) (f : L'.Functions n), Decidable (f ∈ Set.range fun f : L.Functions n => onFunction ϕ f)]     [∀ (n) (r : L'.Relations n), Decidable (r ∈ Set.range fun r : L.Relations n => onRelation ϕ r)]     (M : Type*) [Inhabited M] [L.Structure M] : L'.Structure M where   funMap {n} f xs :=     if h' : f ∈ Set.range fun f : L.Functions n => onFunction ϕ f then funMap h'.choose xs     else default   RelMap {n} r xs :=     if h' : r ∈ Set.range fun r : L.Relations n => onRelation ϕ r then RelMap h'.choose xs     else default
FirstOrder.Language.LHom.defaultExpansio.description: The definition describes a process for extending the structure of one language to another by pulling it along a homomorphism and then arbitrarily expanding it to fit the new language's framework.

explanatories.PEmpty.elim: The elimination of an empty type allows one to derive any type from it, effectively indicating that no values of the empty type exist.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.IsRelational.empty_f: The theorem states that in a relational language, there are no function symbols of any arity.
explanatories.IsEmpty.elim: If a type is empty, then any function defined on that type can be trivially satisfied using any element from that empty type.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.IsAlgebraic.empty_re: The theorem states that if a language is algebraic, then it contains no relation symbols of a given arity.
explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.

FirstOrder.Language.LHom.ofIsEmpty_isExp.description: The definition states that a specific homomorphism derived from the emptiness of one language with respect to another acts as an expansion on a structure that adheres to both languages.

explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LHom.sumElim: The definition outlines a homomorphism that maps elements from a disjoint sum of two languages to a target language, utilizing specified functions for each factor of the sum.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LHom.sumElim_comp_in: The theorem states that composing the sum elimination of a homomorphism with the sum inclusion leads back to the original homomorphism.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LHom.sumElim_inl_inr: The theorem establishes that the homomorphism induced by the left injection of a disjoint sum followed by the elimination homomorphism equals the identity homomorphism on the disjoint sum of two languages.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LHom.comp_sumElim: The theorem establishes that composing a sum elimination homomorphism with another homomorphism is equivalent to applying the composed homomorphisms to the sum of their arguments.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LEquiv.invLHom: The definition specifies a homomorphism that acts as the inverse of a linguistic equivalence between two languages, allowing elements from the second language to be interpreted in terms of the first.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LEquiv.toLHom: The definition describes a function that translates an equivalence between two formal languages into a homomorphism from one language to the other.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LEquiv.right_inv: The theorem states that for any homomorphism between two languages, composing it with its inverse yields the identity homomorphism on the target language.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LEquiv.left_inv: The theorem states that the composition of the inverse homomorphism and the original homomorphism from one language to another results in the identity homomorphism on the original language.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.LEquiv.trans: This definition describes the composition of two equivalences between first-order languages, resulting in a new equivalence that connects the first and third languages through the second.

explanatories.trans: This theorem demonstrates that in a transitive relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second and from the second to the third, it must also hold from the first element to the third.
explanatories.congr: This theorem asserts that if two functions are equal and their corresponding arguments are equal, then applying these functions to these arguments will yield equal results.

explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Theory.model_iff: The theorem establishes that a structure satisfies a theory if and only if it satisfies all formulas contained in that theory.
explanatories.Set.mem_insert_iff: An element belongs to the insertion of an element into a set if and only if it is either that element or an element of the original set.
explanatories.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it is equal to the unique element in that set.
explanatories.forall_eq_or_imp: The universal quantification of a condition leading to a proposition can be expressed as the conjunction of that proposition at a specific point and the same condition leading to the proposition for all points.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Relations.realize_re: The theorem establishes that a relation is reflexive in a given structure if and only if the corresponding relational mapping maintains the reflexivity property for all pairs of elements in that structure.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Structure.relMap_app: The theorem states that the application of a two-ary relation mapping to a pair of elements results in the same value as the binary predicate defined for that relation with the elements as inputs.
explanatories.forall_eq: For any type, if a property holds for all elements equal to a specific element, then it holds for that specific element itself.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Relations.realize_tr: The theorem establishes that a relation is transitive in a structure if and only if the transitive closure defined by that relation holds for all pairs of elements in the structure.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

FirstOrder.Field.FieldAxiom.toProp.fullDefinition: def FieldAxiom.toProp (K : Type*) [Add K] [Mul K] [Neg K] [Zero K] [One K] :     FieldAxiom → Prop   | .addAssoc => ∀ x y z : K, (x + y) + z = x + (y + z)   | .zeroAdd => ∀ x : K, 0 + x = x   | .addLeftNeg => ∀ x : K, -x + x = 0   | .mulAssoc => ∀ x y z : K, (x * y) * z = x * (y * z)   | .mulComm => ∀ x y : K, x * y = y * x   | .oneMul => ∀ x : K, 1 * x = x   | .existsInv => ∀ x : K, x ≠ 0 → ∃ y, x * y = 1   | .leftDistrib => ∀ x y z : K, x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z   | .existsPairNE => ∃ x y : K, x ≠ y

explanatories.Filter.productSetoid: A definition for a setoid that describes the equivalence relations for dependent functions with respect to a given filter, which is used in the context of filter products.

explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Filter.iInter_mem: A theorem that states that the intersection of a finite collection of sets, indexed by a finite type, belongs to a filter if and only if each individual set in the collection belongs to the filter.
explanatories.Set.mem_iInter: An element belongs to the indexed intersection of sets if and only if it is included in every set specified by the indexing collection.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.Filter.inter_mem: A theorem stating that the intersection of two sets belonging to a filter is also a set that belongs to the same filter.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.setoidP.fullDefinition: instance setoidPrestructure : L.Prestructure ((u : Filter α).productSetoid M) :=   { (u : Filter α).productSetoid M with     toStructure :=       { funMap := fun {n} f x a => funMap f fun i => x i a         RelMap := fun {n} r x => ∀ᶠ a : α in u, RelMap r fun i => x i a }     fun_equiv := fun {n} f x y xy => by       refine mem_of_superset (iInter_mem.2 xy) fun a ha => ?_       simp only [Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at ha       simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ha]     rel_equiv := fun {n} r x y xy => by       rw [← iff_eq_eq]       refine ⟨fun hx => ?_, fun hy => ?_⟩       · refine mem_of_superset (inter_mem hx (iInter_mem.2 xy)) ?_         rintro a ⟨ha1, ha2⟩         simp only [Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at *         rw [← funext ha2]         exact ha1       · refine mem_of_superset (inter_mem hy (iInter_mem.2 xy)) ?_         rintro a ⟨ha1, ha2⟩         simp only [Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at *         rw [funext ha2]         exact ha1 }
FirstOrder.Language.Ultraproduct.setoidP.description: The definition describes a structure that organizes a family of types using an ultrafilter to create a prestructure in a formal language framework.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.listE.fullDefinition: def listEncode : ∀ {n : ℕ},     L.BoundedFormula α n → List (Sum (Σk, L.Term (Sum α (Fin k))) (Sum (Σn, L.Relations n) ℕ))   | n, falsum => [Sum.inr (Sum.inr (n + 2))]   | _, equal t₁ t₂ => [Sum.inl ⟨_, t₁⟩, Sum.inl ⟨_, t₂⟩]   | n, rel R ts => [Sum.inr (Sum.inl ⟨_, R⟩), Sum.inr (Sum.inr n)] ++       (List.finRange _).map fun i => Sum.inl ⟨n, ts i⟩   | _, imp φ₁ φ₂ => (Sum.inr (Sum.inr 0)::φ₁.listEncode) ++ φ₂.listEncode   | _, all φ => Sum.inr (Sum.inr 1)::φ.listEncode

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.listD.fullDefinition: def listDecode : ∀ l : List (Sum (Σk, L.Term (Sum α (Fin k))) (Sum (Σn, L.Relations n) ℕ)),     (Σn, L.BoundedFormula α n) ×     { l' : List (Sum (Σk, L.Term (Sum α (Fin k))) (Sum (Σn, L.Relations n) ℕ)) //       SizeOf.sizeOf l' ≤ max 1 (SizeOf.sizeOf l) }   | Sum.inr (Sum.inr (n + 2))::l => ⟨⟨n, falsum⟩, l, le_max_of_le_right le_add_self⟩   | Sum.inl ⟨n₁, t₁⟩::Sum.inl ⟨n₂, t₂⟩::l =>     ⟨if h : n₁ = n₂ then ⟨n₁, equal t₁ (Eq.mp (by rw [h]) t₂)⟩ else default, l, by       simp only [SizeOf.sizeOf, List._sizeOf_1, ← add_assoc]       exact le_max_of_le_right le_add_self⟩   | Sum.inr (Sum.inl ⟨n, R⟩)::Sum.inr (Sum.inr k)::l =>     ⟨if h : ∀ i : Fin n, ((l.map Sum.getLeft?).get? i).join.isSome then         if h' : ∀ i, (Option.get _ (h i)).1 = k then           ⟨k, BoundedFormula.rel R fun i => Eq.mp (by rw [h' i]) (Option.get _ (h i)).2⟩         else default       else default,       l.drop n, le_max_of_le_right (le_add_left (le_add_left (List.drop_sizeOf_le _ _)))⟩   | Sum.inr (Sum.inr 0)::l =>     have : SizeOf.sizeOf         (↑(listDecode l).2 : List (Sum (Σk, L.Term (Sum α (Fin k))) (Sum (Σn, L.Relations n) ℕ))) <         1 + (1 + 1) + SizeOf.sizeOf l := by       refine lt_of_le_of_lt (listDecode l).2.2 (max_lt ?_ (Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left (by decide)))       rw [add_assoc, lt_add_iff_pos_right, add_pos_iff]       exact Or.inl zero_lt_two     ⟨sigmaImp (listDecode l).1 (listDecode (listDecode l).2).1,       (listDecode (listDecode l).2).2,       le_max_of_le_right         (_root_.trans (listDecode _).2.2           (max_le (le_add_right le_self_add)             (_root_.trans (listDecode _).2.2 (max_le (le_add_right le_self_add) le_add_self))))⟩   | Sum.inr (Sum.inr 1)::l =>     ⟨sigmaAll (listDecode l).1, (listDecode l).2,       (listDecode l).2.2.trans (max_le_max le_rfl le_add_self)⟩   | _ => ⟨default, [], le_max_left _ _⟩

explanatories.isGLB_biInf: This theorem asserts that the infimum of the image of a set under a function is the greatest lower bound of that image in a complete lattice.
explanatories.And.left: From a conjunction of two propositions, it is possible to extract and prove the first proposition.
explanatories.And.right: This theorem allows for the extraction of the second component from a conjunction when given a proof of that conjunction.

FirstOrder.Language.Substructure.dense_i.comment:
If `s` is a dense set in a structure `M`, `Substructure.closure L s = ⊤`, then in order to prove
that some predicate `p` holds for all `x : M` it suffices to verify `p x` for `x ∈ s`, and verify

FirstOrder.Language.Embedding.codRestric.fullDefinition: def codRestrict (p : L.Substructure N) (f : M ↪[L] N) (h : ∀ c, f c ∈ p) : M ↪[L] p where   toFun := f.toHom.codRestrict p h   inj' a b ab := f.injective (Subtype.mk_eq_mk.1 ab)   map_fun' {n} F x := (f.toHom.codRestrict p h).map_fun' F x   map_rel' {n} r x := by     simp only     rw [← p.subtype.map_rel]     change RelMap r (Hom.comp p.subtype.toHom (f.toHom.codRestrict p h) ∘ x) ↔ _     rw [Hom.subtype_comp_codRestrict, ← f.map_rel]     rfl

FirstOrder.Language.ElementaryEmbedding.mk.injEq.{u_1, u_2, u_5, u_6} {L : Language} {M : Type u_1} {N : Type u_2}
  [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] (toFun : M → N)
  (map_formula' : ∀ ⦃n : ℕ⦄ (φ : L.Formula (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → M), φ.Realize (toFun ∘ x) ↔ φ.Realize x := by intros;
    trivial) :
  ∀ (toFun_1 : M → N)
    (map_formula'_1 :
      autoParam (∀ ⦃n : ℕ⦄ (φ : L.Formula (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → M), φ.Realize (toFun_1 ∘ x) ↔ φ.Realize x) _auto✝),
    ({ toFun := toFun, map_formula' := map_formula' } = { toFun := toFun_1, map_formula' := map_formula'_1 }) =
      (toFun = toFun_1)

FirstOrder.Language.exists_elementarySub.comment:

If `s` is a set in an `L`-structure `M` and `κ` an infinite cardinal such that
`max (#s, L.card) ≤ κ` and `κ ≤ # M`, then `M` has an elementary substructure containing `s` of
cardinality `κ`.

explanatories.trans: This theorem demonstrates that in a transitive relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second and from the second to the third, it must also hold from the first element to the third.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.setoid: This definition characterizes a setoid that arises from the directed limit of structures, which effectively combines them along given embeddings within a specified language framework.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.sigmaStr: This definition specifies the creation of a structure on a dependent sum type that represents the structure of the direct limit after applying a quotient process.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.exists_u: This theorem asserts the existence of an index in a directed system such that the unified values of two equivalent dependent pairs can be shown to be equal at that index using specified upper bounds.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.funMap_e: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the application of a function to a sequence of structures and the construction of a sigma structure from those functions combined with a unifying process, given certain bounds within the index set.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.relMap_e: This theorem establishes an equivalence in interpreting relations on a collection of structures, showing that a relational mapping on these structures is consistent with a unified representation when focusing on a specific index within the directed system.
explanatories.Setoid.trans: If two elements are related by a relation and the second element is related to a third element, then the first and third elements are also related by the same relation.
explanatories.Setoid.symm: The symmetry property of an equivalence relation asserts that if one element is equivalent to another, then the second element is also equivalent to the first.
explanatories.symm: This theorem establishes that if a binary relation is symmetric, then holding the relation between two elements implies that it also holds in the reverse order between those elements.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Equiv.symm: The definition states that the inverse of a first-order equivalence between two structures is also a first-order equivalence.

FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.prestruc.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance prestructure : L.Prestructure (DirectLimit.setoid G f) where   toStructure := sigmaStructure G f   fun_equiv {n} {F} x y xy := by     obtain ⟨i, hx, hy, h⟩ := exists_unify_eq G f xy     refine       Setoid.trans (funMap_equiv_unify G f F x i hx)         (Setoid.trans ?_ (Setoid.symm (funMap_equiv_unify G f F y i hy)))     rw [h]   rel_equiv {n} {R} x y xy := by     obtain ⟨i, hx, hy, h⟩ := exists_unify_eq G f xy     refine _root_.trans (relMap_equiv_unify G f R x i hx)       (_root_.trans ?_ (symm (relMap_equiv_unify G f R y i hy)))     rw [h]

FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.of.fullDefinition: def of (i : ι) : G i ↪[L] DirectLimit G f where   toFun := fun a => ⟦.mk f i a⟧   inj' x y h := by     rw [Quotient.eq] at h     obtain ⟨j, h1, _, h3⟩ := h     exact (f i j h1).injective h3   map_fun' F x := by     simp only     rw [← funMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk']     rfl   map_rel' := by     intro n R x     change RelMap R (fun a => (⟦.mk f i (x a)⟧ : DirectLimit G f)) ↔ _     simp only [relMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk']

  [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => ⇑(f i j h)] [Nonempty ι] {P : Type u₁} [L.Structure P] (g : (i : ι) → G i ↪[L] P)

FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.lift.comment:
The universal property of the direct limit: maps from the components to another module
that respect the directed system structure (i.e. make some diagram commute) give rise
to a unique map out of the direct limit.

FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.lift.fullDefinition: def lift : DirectLimit G f ↪[L] P where   toFun :=     Quotient.lift (fun x : Σˣ f => (g x.1) x.2) fun x y xy => by       simp only       obtain ⟨i, hx, hy⟩ := directed_of (· ≤ ·) x.1 y.1       rw [← Hg x.1 i hx, ← Hg y.1 i hy]       exact congr_arg _ ((equiv_iff ..).1 xy)   inj' x y xy := by     rw [← Quotient.out_eq x, ← Quotient.out_eq y, Quotient.lift_mk, Quotient.lift_mk] at xy     obtain ⟨i, hx, hy⟩ := directed_of (· ≤ ·) x.out.1 y.out.1     rw [← Hg x.out.1 i hx, ← Hg y.out.1 i hy] at xy     rw [← Quotient.out_eq x, ← Quotient.out_eq y, Quotient.eq, equiv_iff G f hx hy]     exact (g i).injective xy   map_fun' F x := by     obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := exists_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk'_eq G f x     change _ = funMap F (Quotient.lift _ _ ∘ Quotient.mk _ ∘ Structure.Sigma.mk f i ∘ y)     rw [funMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk', ← Function.comp.assoc, Quotient.lift_comp_mk]     simp only [Quotient.lift_mk, Embedding.map_fun]     rfl   map_rel' R x := by     obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := exists_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk'_eq G f x     change RelMap R (Quotient.lift _ _ ∘ Quotient.mk _ ∘ Structure.Sigma.mk f i ∘ y) ↔ _     rw [relMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk' G f, ← (g i).map_rel R y, ← Function.comp.assoc,       Quotient.lift_comp_mk]     rfl
FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.lift.description: This definition describes a way to lift a structure from a directed system to its direct limit, preserving the mapping properties of the direct system in a unique manner.

first_order.language.direct_limit.lift.fullDefinition: def lift : DirectLimit G f ↪[L] P where   toFun :=     Quotient.lift (fun x : Σˣ f => (g x.1) x.2) fun x y xy => by       simp only       obtain ⟨i, hx, hy⟩ := directed_of (· ≤ ·) x.1 y.1       rw [← Hg x.1 i hx, ← Hg y.1 i hy]       exact congr_arg _ ((equiv_iff ..).1 xy)   inj' x y xy := by     rw [← Quotient.out_eq x, ← Quotient.out_eq y, Quotient.lift_mk, Quotient.lift_mk] at xy     obtain ⟨i, hx, hy⟩ := directed_of (· ≤ ·) x.out.1 y.out.1     rw [← Hg x.out.1 i hx, ← Hg y.out.1 i hy] at xy     rw [← Quotient.out_eq x, ← Quotient.out_eq y, Quotient.eq, equiv_iff G f hx hy]     exact (g i).injective xy   map_fun' F x := by     obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := exists_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk'_eq G f x     change _ = funMap F (Quotient.lift _ _ ∘ Quotient.mk _ ∘ Structure.Sigma.mk f i ∘ y)     rw [funMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk', ← Function.comp.assoc, Quotient.lift_comp_mk]     simp only [Quotient.lift_mk, Embedding.map_fun]     rfl   map_rel' R x := by     obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := exists_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk'_eq G f x     change RelMap R (Quotient.lift _ _ ∘ Quotient.mk _ ∘ Structure.Sigma.mk f i ∘ y) ↔ _     rw [relMap_quotient_mk'_sigma_mk' G f, ← (g i).map_rel R y, ← Function.comp.assoc,       Quotient.lift_comp_mk]     rfl

  [(i : ι) → L.Structure (G i)] {f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j} [IsDirected ι fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1]
  [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => ⇑(f i j h)] [Nonempty ι] {P : Type u₁} [L.Structure P] (g : (i : ι) → G i ↪[L] P)

  (lift L ι G f g Hg) ((of L ι G f i) x) = (g i) x

FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.equiv_li.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equiv_lift : DirectLimit G f ≃[L] DirectLimit G' f' := by   let U i : G i ↪[L] DirectLimit G' f' := (of L _ G' f' i).comp (g i).toEmbedding   let F : DirectLimit G f ↪[L] DirectLimit G' f' := lift L _ G f U <| by     intro _ _ _ _     simp only [U, Embedding.comp_apply, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, H_commuting, of_f]   have surj_f : Function.Surjective F := by     intro x     rcases x with ⟨i, pre_x⟩     use of L _ G f i ((g i).symm pre_x)     simp only [F, U, lift_of, Embedding.comp_apply, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]     rfl   exact ⟨Equiv.ofBijective F ⟨F.injective, surj_f⟩, F.map_fun', F.map_rel'⟩
FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.equiv_li.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the direct limits of two isomorphic families of structures, demonstrating how the structures relate through a series of specified bijections.

FirstOrder.Language.exists_countable_is_age_of_iff.{u, v, w} {L : Language} {K : Set (Bundled L.Structure)}
  [Countable ((l : ℕ) × L.Functions l)] :
  (∃ M, Countable ↑M ∧ L.age ↑M = K) ↔
    K.Nonempty ∧
      (∀ (M N : Bundled L.Structure), Nonempty (↑M ≃[L] ↑N) → (M ∈ K ↔ N ∈ K)) ∧
        (Quotient.mk' '' K).Countable ∧ (∀ M ∈ K, Structure.FG L ↑M) ∧ Hereditary K ∧ JointEmbedding K

FirstOrder.Language.exists_countable_is_.description: There exists a countable structure whose age is a given set if and only if that set is non-empty, each structure within it is isomorphic to the others if they are in the same class, it can be partitioned into a countable set of equivalence classes, every structure in the set is finitely generated, the set is hereditary, and has the joint embedding property.

FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous.code: FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous.{u, v, w} (L : Language) (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] : Prop
FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous.comment:
A structure `M` is ultrahomogeneous if every embedding of a finitely generated substructure
into `M` extends to an automorphism of `M`.

explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Embedding.comp: This definition describes the composition of first-order embeddings, which allows the creation of a new embedding from one structure to another by combining two existing embeddings.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Substructure.subtype: This definition represents the natural embedding of a substructure into its parent structure in the context of a formal language.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.FirstOrder.Language.Hom.comp: The definition describes the composition of two homomorphisms in first-order logic, resulting in a new homomorphism from the first structure to the third structure.

FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous.fullDefinition: def IsUltrahomogeneous : Prop :=   ∀ (S : L.Substructure M) (_ : S.FG) (f : S ↪[L] M),     ∃ g : M ≃[L] M, f = g.toEmbedding.comp S.subtype
FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous.description: A structure is ultrahomogeneous if every embedding of its finitely generated substructures can be extended to an automorphism of the entire structure.
